specAnchors.text: CORE PRACTICAL 7 The oxidation of propan-1-ol to produce propanal and propanoic acid. Further suggested practical: Investigation of reactions of primary and secondary alcohols, including propan-1-ol and propan-2-ol

primer.text: One alcohol, two destinations. This core practical drips propan-1-ol into cooled acidified dichromate, distilling propanal before it over-oxidises or refluxing to propanoic acid, then closes with the hazard ledger: flammable alcohols, an oxidising reagent, and the precautions that keep both tame.

modules.title: Core Practical 7: from propan-1-ol to propanal and beyond
sourceHeadings: Synthesis and purification of propanal and propanoic acid
modules.opening: This core practical turns propan-1-ol into propanal, or all the way to propanoic acid, using acidified dichromate. The technique controls how far the oxidation climbs: dropwise addition into cooled oxidant, reflux for the acid, or distillation for the aldehyde, followed by purification.
keyPoints: Primary alcohols oxidise to aldehydes, which oxidise further to carboxylic acids; propan-1-ol gives propanal then propanoic acid.
20 cm3 of acidified potassium dichromate solution is cooled in an iced water bath inside a 50 cm3 pear-shaped flask.
Anti-bumping granules are added, and 1 cm3 of propan-1-ol is dripped slowly into the reflux condenser by pipette.
After warming to room temperature the mixture is heated for 20 minutes by electric heater or water bath, never a naked flame.
The product is purified by distillation, collecting the propanal fraction, or refluxed with excess oxidant for the acid.

low.restatement: Cool the oxidant, drip the alcohol in slowly, then heat without flames: distil promptly for the aldehyde or keep refluxing with excess oxidant for the acid, purifying the product afterwards by distillation.
low.analogy: A climbing route with a mid-station: leave the train at propanal by distilling early, or ride on to propanoic acid by staying in the reflux carriage.
low.examPointer: Quote the dropwise addition, the iced bath and the flame-free heating as the three control measures in practical-plan answers.

medium.restatement: The dropwise addition into cooled dichromate keeps the alcohol's residence time short so the aldehyde stage is caught; continuing to reflux hands the aldehyde more contact with the oxidant, driving it to the acid; distillation then separates whichever product was targeted by its boiling point.
medium.analogy: A conveyor belt: short rides stop at the first station (propanal), long rides continue to the terminal (propanoic acid).
medium.examPointer: Explain why the ice bath matters - the exothermic oxidation and volatile alcohol both demand temperature control from the start.

modules.title: Hazards in the oxidation laboratory
modules.opening: Every reagent in this practical carries a warning label. The alcohols are flammable and harmful, the dichromate is a strong oxidising agent, and the routine answers are fume cupboards, water-mopping of spillages and distance from naked flames.
keyPoints: The alcohols used, such as propan-1-ol, butan-1-ol and pentan-1-ol, are flammable and often harmful to health.
Alcohols must be kept away from naked flames such as Bunsen burners.
Skin contact and inhalation of vapour should be avoided, with a fume cupboard used for harmful alcohols.
Potassium dichromate is a strong oxidising agent requiring careful handling.
Spillages should be mopped up immediately with plenty of water.

low.restatement: Match each hazard to its control: flames off for flammable alcohols, fume cupboard for harmful vapours, careful handling and water mopping for the oxidising dichromate.
low.analogy: A fire triangle map: remove the ignition source, contain the vapour, and wash away the spill before any of them meet.
low.examPointer: In risk-assessment answers pair every named reagent with its specific precaution rather than a generic 'be careful'.

medium.restatement: The hazard logic chains: volatile flammable alcohols need an ignition-free heating route and vapour control; a strong oxidant like dichromate intensifies any fire it meets, so it is stored and handled away from combustibles, and spillages are diluted fast to defuse both hazards at once.
medium.analogy: Keeping matches away from petrol cans, with a hose ready: the same separation and response logic runs this bench.
medium.examPointer: Justify the water-mopping response as dilution of both a flammable vapour source and an oxidising concentrate.

glossary.definition: The aldehyde from oxidising propan-1-ol once, boiling lower than its parent alcohol.
The carboxylic acid from oxidising propanal further under reflux with excess oxidant.
Inert granules that give nucleation sites for smooth boiling in heated flasks.
